summary: myidsan gains an in-app config editor over a safe subset of config.json — localAuth, sso, security, storage, logging — the last of the four apps to get one, ported and adapted from myseliasan's settings feature. This change is backend/API only: GET /api/settings, GET/PUT /api/settings/{section}, POST /api/settings/{section}/reset, and POST /api/settings/cache/test are superadmin-only (enforced as route-group middleware, matching audit/backup/mfa-admin), and a save writes the changed leaves back into config.json (every other block preserved byte-for-byte) and reports needsRestart. The security section is the standout: it surfaces the lockout, password-policy, and MFA-policy blocks through their resolved Effective*() values, so an operator can finally see what those absent-from-config blocks resolve to instead of a misleading zero/off reading, with validation floors (maxAttempts >= 2 once lockout is on, minLength >= 8, a known mfa.policy value). audit.retention is deliberately not exposed — the audit trail's only removal path stays config-file-only on purpose, so the superadmin whose actions it records cannot reach the knob from inside the product — and neither are kerberos or login.oidc[]/social providers. Unlike myseliasan's port, there is no server-side file-browse endpoint, since myidsan is the identity provider and the highest-value target in the suite; the sso section only exposes the provider (issuing) side of the shared config block, and authCodeTtlSeconds is capped at 600 seconds. Saves/resets are recorded in the audit trail (section and actor only, never values). The React Settings page itself is not part of this change and remains outstanding.
compatibility: Adds a new superadmin-only API surface and one new seeded endpoint row + System-group nav item ("Settings"); no existing behavior changes for any current install, and no new config keys are required — every editable section already has defaults. Saving through the new API still requires a process restart to take effect, exactly like every other infra-block edit on this app. Nil-database construction is now supported (disables only the reset-to-defaults snapshot), so no migration or first-boot cost is imposed on existing databases.
